name: Zambra

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A local flamenco historian or dancer from Granada
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

narration: The Secret Dance of the Sacromonte Caves
This is Zambra. 16th century to present.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated from the Romani people of Granada and Almería, evolving from earlier Morisco dance styles.
It was suppressed during the 16th-century Inquisition but continued to be practiced in secret.
on_screen: Map: Spain · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Historically, the Zambra was a staple of Romani wedding ceremonies.
It is now frequently performed as a cultural attraction in the caves of Granada.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: VID 20201020120321 (https://archive.org/details/vid-20201020120321)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform barefoot, utilizing finger cymbals.
The movement is characterized by a slow, heavy rhythm with similarities to belly dancing, focusing on the fluidity of the skirt.
Watch for Hip-led movement.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (scMES7MqlcU)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Small, intimate spaces like caves
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is typically a slow, binary-meter flamenco style, often described as a slow tango.
Key instruments include the guitar and sonajas (finger cymbals).
Listen for the guitar, sonajas (finger cymbals).
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4.
A slow, heavy flamenco rhythm characterized by arabizing melodies and the metallic clatter of finger cymbals.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: La zambra flamenca — José María Velázquez-Gaztelu

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wear a blouse tied under the bust and a long skirt fitted at the hips with wide pleats.
It is traditionally performed in the caves of Sacromonte.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Carmen Amaya, Lola Flores, Manolo Caracol, La Chunga, and Pilar López Júlvez are recognized for adopting and popularizing the style.
The dance is primarily associated with the Sacromonte district in Granada and the cave dwellings of Almería.
The dance is considered a descendant of Morisco dance traditions, later assimilated by Romani groups.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: A slow, heavy flamenco rhythm characterized by arabizing melodies and the metallic clatter of finger cymbals.
listen_before_composing: La zambra flamenca — José María Velázquez-Gaztelu
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Zambra (Spain). Meter 2/4 or 4/4. Rhythm pattern: Slow tango-like rhythm. Instruments: guitar, sonajas (finger cymbals). Mood: arabizing, slow, sensual. It should sound like this: A slow, heavy flamenco rhythm characterized by arabizing melodies and the metallic clatter of finger cymbals. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred
wardrobe.from_sources: Performers wear a blouse tied under the bust and a long skirt fitted at the hips with wide pleats. It is traditionally performed in the caves of Sacromonte.
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction
